title: Skill Stacking
equation: Unique Advantage = Skill A × Skill B × Skill C × Personal Context
hook: You don't have to be the best in the world at one thing. An odd combo of good skills works too.
statement: Mixing unrelated skills can give you an edge competitors can't easily copy.
explainer: Plenty of people are great at one thing. Very few have your exact mix of skills and experiences. That combination is hard to hire away and hard to copy. It's your personal moat.
sop: Find where they overlap in ways others couldn't copy.
Build an offer, role, or brand around that overlap.
Score Skill A, Skill B, Skill C, and Personal Context, then improve the weakest.
equation_example: Skill A 8, Skill B 6, Skill C 7, Personal Context 9. 8 × 6 × 7 × 9 = 3,024 Unique Advantage, out of 10,000. Higher means your combo is tough to copy or replace. Lower means someone cheaper could step into any one piece.
question: Write down your three strongest skills and one offer only someone with all three could make.
closing_statement: Your edge is the combination, not the skill.
caption:
Principle Nº 266: Skill Stacking

You don't have to be the best in the world at one thing. An odd combo of good skills works too.

Mixing unrelated skills can give you an edge competitors can't easily copy.
